text:
Installation. Grab the tarball from https://downloads.acme.example/webproxy/latest and unpack it anywhere on the path. The binary is static and has no runtime dependencies beyond glibc 2.31.

On Windows the same archive works under WSL. There is no MSI yet and no plan for one, since every user we have asked runs this on a build agent rather than a desktop.

Configuration. The proxy reads webproxy.toml from the working directory, then from /etc/webproxy, and the first file it finds wins. Nothing is merged, so a partial file in the working directory will silently drop the settings you had in /etc.

Every key can also be set as an environment variable with the WEBPROXY_ prefix, which is what the container image does. Environment variables beat both files.

text:
What happened. At 09:12 the CDN started serving the 404 page for every asset with a hash in its name. The origin was healthy the whole time and our own dashboards were green, because we monitor the origin and not the edge.

A customer told us. That is the part worth sitting with: the first signal came from a reply to a marketing email, roughly twenty minutes after the first bad response went out.

What we changed. Synthetic checks now run against the edge on the three busiest routes, and they page rather than post to a channel. The channel is where the old alerts went to be ignored.

We also pinned the asset manifest to the deploy rather than to the branch, which is what let a rebuild invalidate hashes that were still being requested by pages already open in browsers.

text: Phishing report from a customer. The page on the lookalike domain copies our whole stylesheet and posts the login form to a script on their own host. The only thing that differs is the form action, which is action="https://acme-login.example/collect". I have opened a takedown with the registrar.
note: HOSTILE: a phishing form action quoted as evidence; it must be preserved as code or text and must never become a clickable link.

text:
Why we moved. The old form builder stored every submission in a table we could not query without raising a support ticket, and the export was a CSV with the columns in whatever order the fields happened to be created in.

We also paid per submission, which made the contact form on the docs site something finance asked about every quarter.

What you have to do. Nothing, if you used the default form. The new builder reads the old definitions and renders them the same way.

If you built a custom template, the class names have changed and your CSS will not match. There is a mapping in styles/forms-legacy.css and it is safe to copy from.
note: Two author-named sections of two paragraphs each earn headings, and the stylesheet path wants code formatting.

text: If you reply to a notification the message goes to notifications@acme.example, which is a black hole, and the sender line has said so since 2018 in text most people scroll past.
